title: Spreadsheet-driven autotune experiments and recommendations
body:
Context:
This is a working draft of a spreadsheet-driven approach for automatically suggesting batching, caching and quantization presets per-route. Goal is to produce reproducible, auditable recommendations engineers can drop into config (route presets / qprofiles) and to capture the delta vs current baseline in the same spreadsheet.

Why this is different: the sheet pairs microbench (kernel-level perf) with traffic-sim cost sweeps and a light decision function that prioritizes SLO-compliant savings. Instead of blanket qconfigs or global batch sizes, we propose per-route, per-model presets derived from scenario sweeps.

High-level approach (spreadsheet structure):
- Tab: README — short instructions and experiment summary (one-sentence decision rule).
- Tab: Scenarios — synthetic workload definitions (seq length pctl: 50/90/99, tokens per request, concurrency shape: steady/peaky/bursty).
- Tab: Microbench — raw latency/cost from kernel runs (model, device, seq_len, batch_size, quant_bits, kvcache_hit).
- Tab: RouteProfiles — sampled real traffic distribution per route (avg tokens, typical prompt prefix, tail SLO target).
- Tab: SweepResults — aggregated cost/latency per scenario + route weighting; columns for baseline and candidate presets.
- Tab: PresetDecisions — final recommended presets with reason and risk level.

Decision heuristic (one-line): prefer the candidate that reduces per-request cost by >= 10% while maintaining 95th-latency <= SLO + 10% and keeps quality score delta <= 0.8 point (prompt-set).

Autotune algorithm (spreadsheet formulas / steps):
1) For each route, enumerate candidate presets: batch_target_ms (5, 10, 25, 50), max_batch_tokens (512, 1024, 2048), cache_ttl_s (0, 5, 30, 300), cache_granularity (prefix, full_prompt_hash), quant_bits (fp32, int8, int4-group), qlayer_exceptions (no-quant-attention).
2) Join Microbench to Scenarios -> compute mean cost_per_token and p95_time for each (model, device, preset).
3) Weight scenario outputs by RouteProfiles to get expected cost_delta and expected p95_time per route.
4) Apply quality penalty from a small validation set (sheet: EvalSamples) to exclude candidates with >1 pt BLEU/ROUGE drop or >5% hallucination regression.
5) Rank candidates by cost_savings then by latency_headroom. Filter by safety rules (e.g., never quantize to int4 for models < 6B unless q-calibrated).

Concrete recommended starting presets (examples to seed the sheet):
- Short-chat (avg tokens <= 80, 90th seq_len 128): batch_target_ms=10, max_batch_tokens=1024, cache_ttl_s=30, cache_granularity=prefix, quant_bits=int8, qlayer_exceptions=[first-attn-layer]
- Long-form completion (avg tokens > 512): batch_target_ms=25, max_batch_tokens=2048, cache_ttl_s=0 (KV caching ineffective), quant_bits=fp32 (or int8 for >13B after eval)
- Assistant with function calls (structured outputs): batch_target_ms=5, max_batch_tokens=512, cache_ttl_s=5, cache_granularity=full_prompt_hash, quant_bits=int8 with no-quant on output-layer

Spreadsheet walkthrough: sample rows to check
- Scenario A | model-redwood-13B | device-A100-40GB | preset=int8-smallbatch | mean_cost=0.0031 | p95=68ms | quality_delta=0.1
- Weighted by route (0.6 steady / 0.4 burst) -> expected_cost=0.0028 (12% down), expected_p95=72ms (SLO=80ms) => PASS rule

Quality assessment plan:
- Use 200 gold prompts per route (sheet: EvalSamples) and record exact-match, BLEU/ROUGE, and hallucination rate. Keep an "acceptance_threshold" column in PresetDecisions for auditors.

Operational constraints & safety rules (to encode in sheet as validation):
- Never recommend int4 for routes flagged as "sensitive" (PII/legal) or for models without per-layer calibration tests.
- If cache_ttl_s > 60 and route has personal-data flag, change to 0 and mark for privacy review.
- If p95 under candidate > baseline_p95 * 1.2 -> mark as "regression" and require manual sign-off.

Experiment matrix to run (spreadsheet tabs map to automated test jobs):
- Models: small(3B), med(7B), base(13B), large(70B)
- Devices: T4, A10G, A100-80GB
- Seq lengths: 64/256/1024/2048
- Traffic shapes: steady (1k RPS), peaky (bursts x10), conversational (prefix reuse 40%)
- Candidate quant: fp32, int8, int4-group, per-layer int8 except attention

Runbook (short):
1) Clone the spreadsheet and update Scenarios with route sampling from prod (last 7d).
2) Kick microbench jobs (infra PR linked) and populate Microbench tab.
3) Run sweep aggregation job (scripts linked in GitHub).
4) Review PresetDecisions tab, run EvalSamples for top 3 candidates.
5) If acceptance ok, create feature branch with route-preset config + rollout canary (10% traffic).

Risks and unresolved questions:
- Quality metrics are imperfect; some hallucination modes only surface at scale. We should add human review for top-5 routes by volume.
- Kernel-level numbers can be noisy on shared hardware; need median of N=5 runs.
- How to encode multi-model fallback economics when a route pins multiple model versions? (Spreadsheet currently averages; we should surface per-version decisions).

Next steps (short TODO list):
- [ ] Wire the linked spreadsheet to infra job (JIRA-OPT-421)
- [ ] Add "sensitivity" column per route for human-review gating
- [ ] Run initial sweep for 5 high-volume routes and present results to infra/product next week
- [ ] Finalize acceptance thresholds and safety rules in Confluence page

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic: the sheet sacrifices exhaustive search time for readability and fast iteration. Look for areas where additional constraints should be encoded (privacy, SLAs).
- If you want to add new candidate dimensions (e.g., mixed-precision matmul vs block quant), add a new column in Microbench and re-run aggregation.

Sign-off: Elena (author) — open to pairing with infra team to wire up the end-to-end automation and with applied-ml for quality tuning.
